title: A lazy value created once, even when first calls race

blocks.text: A lazy Singleton creates its object on first use. The page's warning is that two threads calling `getInstance()` for the first time at once can each see "not created yet" and each build one. **Double-checked locking** fixes it: check without the lock, then take the lock and **check again** before creating, with **the field holding the value declared `volatile`** (a field of type `T`), so no thread sees a half-built object.
Write `Lazy<T>`, the same idea for any value:

items: `Lazy.of(supplier)` returns a holder and **creates nothing yet**.
`get()` calls the supplier on the first call and returns that object from every call after it.
Even when threads race on the first `get()`, **the supplier runs once** and every thread gets the same object.

rows: thread A and thread B call `get()` together

cases.says: get() calls the supplier once and returns that same object from every later call.
Lazy.of() does not call the supplier; only the first get() does.
When a second thread calls get() while the first is still inside the supplier, the supplier still runs once and both threads get the same object.
A thread that waited for the lock finds the value already made and does not call the supplier again.
Lazy keeps the value in a field of type T, and that field is volatile.

concepts: A lazy Singleton creates its instance on first use, and concurrent first calls must still create only one, which double-checked locking does by checking again inside the lock.
